page.title: Hoher Kasten Ridge Walk (1795 m) — Hike Plan

hero.subtitle_html: Ridge walk from Brülisau — SAC T2 · ~1000 m gain · ~8 km · ~4–5 h · cable car option

intro_html:
"Hoher Kasten is the most prominent viewpoint of the Appenzell Alps — a 360° panorama encompassing the Rhine valley, the Bodensee, the Säntis massif, and the Vorarlberg mountains of Austria. The revolving restaurant at the summit turns the hard work optional."
— Appenzell tourism descriptions

Hoher Kasten (1795 m) is the flagship summit of Appenzell Ausserrhoden, reached either on foot from Brülisau (~1000 m gain, T2, ~3 h) or via the Luftseilbahn Brülisau–Hoher Kasten cable car (year-round). The classic objective is the ridge traverse towards Staubern (1635 m) and onward towards Saxer Lücke — a spectacular T2 walk with open views in all directions and almost no crowds once you leave the summit. Very popular on summer weekends; an early start or a shoulder-season visit rewards you with solitude.
quick_facts: ~8 km · ridge traverse to Staubern and back
Bodensee, Rhine valley, Säntis, Vorarlberg, Bavarian Alps (clear days)

routes_subtitle: (T2 hiking routes — SAC mountain hiking grade)

routes.title_html: 1. Cable car + ridge traverse — recommended classic
bullets_html: Take the Luftseilbahn Brülisau–Hoher Kasten from Brülisau (year-round, ~10 min).
From the summit, follow the marked ridge trail south-west towards Staubern (1635 m, ~45 min one-way).
Continue ridge towards Saxer Lücke if time allows — the ridge opens up with views of both Appenzell valleys.
Return to Hoher Kasten by the same ridge; cable car down, or hike down to Brülisau.
Total ridge walking: ~4–5 km, ~2–3 h on the ridge itself.

routes.title_html: 2. Full ascent from Brülisau on foot — T2
bullets_html: Start at Brülisau (~780 m); well-marked trail via Rohr alp ascending the south flank.
Ascent ~1000 m gain, ~3 h to summit.
Well-maintained hiking path, T2 throughout — steeper upper section but never exposed.
Descend via the same route or via the ridge to Staubern and down to Brülisau or Saxer Lücke.

routes.title_html: 3. Loop via Saxer Lücke — full day
bullets_html: Cable car up to Hoher Kasten; ridge traverse to Staubern then Saxer Lücke (~1652 m).
Descend from Saxer Lücke into the inner Appenzell valley or back towards Brülisau.
Total loop distance: ~12–14 km depending on variant; ~5–6 h.
Outstanding views throughout; stay alert for cattle on the open ridge.

getting_there.by_pt_html:
• Train: Zürich HB → St. Gallen (IC, ~70 min).
  • Appenzell Bahn: St. Gallen → Appenzell (~45 min).
  • Postbus: Appenzell → Brülisau (~20 min, line 222).
  • Total journey: ~2 h from Zürich. Plan via sbb.ch.
  • Cable car: Luftseilbahn Brülisau–Hoher Kasten runs year-round from Brülisau village.
getting_there.by_car_html: Drive to Brülisau (Appenzell Ausserrhoden). Parking at the cable car valley station. From Zürich: ~1.5 h via A1 → St. Gallen → Appenzell road.

day_plans.title: Day Plan — Cable Car Up + Ridge Walk
rows: Cable car up to Hoher Kasten summit (1795 m), ~10 min
Staubern (~1635 m) — views south into Appenzell Innerrhoden
Back at Hoher Kasten summit — coffee/lunch at the Drehrestaurant
Cable car down (or hike down, ~1.5–2 h)
day_plans.footer_html: Full hike-up variant: start at ~08:30 in Brülisau, allow ~3 h ascent. Aim to summit before 13:00 to avoid afternoon thunderstorms.

day_plans.title: Day Plan — Full Loop via Saxer Lücke
rows: Ridge traverse: Hoher Kasten → Staubern → Saxer Lücke (~1652 m), ~1.5 h
Saxer Lücke — optional: continue to Fählensee
Descend towards Brülisau or inner Appenzell valley
Back at Brülisau (~5–6 h loop total)
day_plans.footer_html: Best suited to longer summer days (June–September). Carry enough water — no reliable sources on the ridge.

lapse_rate.example_html: Example: Appenzell forecast 16–24 °C → Hoher Kasten summit ≈ 10 °C to 18 °C. Wind on the exposed ridge can make it feel significantly colder.

sources_html: MeteoSwiss — use the Appenzell or Brülisau point forecast for best accuracy.
Meteoblue Appenzell — hourly forecast + nearby webcam links.
Thunderstorms in the afternoon are common in summer — aim to be off the exposed ridge by 13:00.
weather.season_html: Year-round accessible via cable car, but ridge walking is best from May to October. Snow and ice can make the ridge slippery in winter even at this modest elevation.

takeaways_html: The cable car is the most popular approach and justifies itself even for fit hikers — it's the ridge traverse that makes the day, not the ascent slog.
The ridge between Hoher Kasten and Staubern is well-marked, wide, and almost entirely T2 — a genuine family-friendly alpine walk with big views.
Arrive early on summer weekends: the summit restaurant and cable car both get very busy by 11:00. A Tuesday morning in August can feel like a private mountain.
On clear days the Bodensee is unmistakable to the north; the Säntis (2502 m) stands immediately to the south-east — a dramatic contrast in scale.

reports.title: Hoher Kasten – Staubern ridge traverse (T2)
bullets_html: Cable car from Brülisau to the summit; immediate views of the Rhine valley and Bodensee.
Ridge walk SW to Staubern (1635 m) is an easy T2 — wide path, gentle gradients, open views on both sides.
Return to summit for lunch at the Drehrestaurant; cable car down in time for the afternoon Postbus.

reports.title: Brülisau → Hoher Kasten on foot — the forgotten approach
bullets_html: Full ascent from Brülisau village (~780 m) via marked trail — ~1000 m gain, ~3 h, T2 throughout.
Upper section steeper but straightforward; trail well-maintained and easy to follow.
Far fewer hikers than the cable car crowd; summit arrival feels genuinely earned.

reports.title: Hoher Kasten – Staubern – Saxer Lücke full loop
bullets_html: Cable car up, then the full ridge to Saxer Lücke (~1652 m) — the Alpstein unfolds ridge by ridge.
Descent from Saxer Lücke into Brülisau or onward into Appenzell Innerrhoden for a point-to-point.
Carry 2–3 L water — no reliable sources on the open ridge. Total ~12–14 km, ~5–6 h.

gear.title: Mandatory
items_html: 2–3 L water (no sources on the ridge)
Phone with offline SwissTopo map + GPX
Cash / card for cable car and restaurant

gear.title: Recommended
items_html: Binoculars (Bodensee and Bavarian Alps on clear days)

safety_html: Exposure: The ridge is broad and T2, but the summit plateau is exposed to wind — dress accordingly.
Thunderstorms: Afternoon storms develop rapidly in summer; be off the ridge by 13:00 if convection is forecast.
Cattle: Open ridge pastures have cattle — give space, especially mothers with calves.
Cable car: Check operating hours and last descent before setting out — see hoherkasten.ch for schedules.
Phone reception: Generally good on the summit; can be patchy on the lower ridge.
Winter visit: the ridge can be icy even at 1700–1800 m; microspikes recommended outside summer season.
